Remove state changes that are not related to the device having a new uptime.
Epoch time (old way of reporting uptime by UniFi) only needs to trigger state change when it has increased.
Uptime in seconds should only trigger state change when smaller than what previously has been reported.

issue_context.title: UniFi uptime sensor is changing a few milli (or micro) seconds now and then
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The uptime sensor of an network device changes by a few milliseconds:

This is the current uptime value: 
 2021-04-20T13:26:24.718558+02:00 

After waiting for 1 minute:
 2021-04-20T13:26:24.441237+02:00 

After waiting for another minute:
 2021-04-20T13:26:24.918208+02:00 

I think this has something to do with the time keeping/time formatting system that is randomly picking milliseconds during formatting.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.4.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.4.2 or core-2021.4.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

UniFi

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

Hey there @kane610, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`unifi`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L508) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
And this is an issue other than to calm an OCD? :)

Nope, it triggers Node-RED everytime it is updated. Now you could say that's Node-REDs issue, but in my opinion this wastes CPU, since Home Assistant might do the same when an automation is created using this timestamp

EDIT: It seems that it also varies by a few seconds sometimes
@Kane610 please see the details I added to https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/51029 it's causing my browser to lock up and crash.
Its always going to wobble since there is a delay between when the data is fetched and when its calculated.

```python
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/unifi/sensor.py b/homeassistant/components/unifi/sensor.py
index c823860285..4f1d32cd4f 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/unifi/sensor.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/unifi/sensor.py
@@ -148,8 +148,17 @@ class UniFiUpTimeSensor(UniFiClient, SensorEntity):
     def state(self) -> datetime:
         """Return the uptime of the client."""
         if self.client.uptime < 1000000000:
-            return (dt_util.now() - timedelta(seconds=self.client.uptime)).isoformat()
-        return dt_util.utc_from_timestamp(float(self.client.uptime)).isoformat()
+            uptime = dt_util.now() - timedelta(seconds=self.client.uptime)
+        uptime = dt_util.utc_from_timestamp(float(self.client.uptime))
+        return uptime.replace(microseconds=0).isoformat()
+
+    @property
+    def entity_registry_enabled_default(self):
+        """Return false to disable this entity by default.
+
+        Timestamp sensors are a drag on the state machine
+        """
+        return False
 
     async def options_updated(self) -> None:
         """Config entry options are updated, remove entity if option is disabled."""

```

Maybe disable them by default?

> Its always going to wobble since there is a delay between when the data is fetched and when its calculated.

Could this not be solved by rounding it? I'd rather it wobble between 33s and 34s vs all the microwobbles.
Also could we check the last state? Maybe if it's only changed by less than 2s we return the old value?
I'm think of storing the time stamp and only update when there is a major difference in size
@Kane610 I think that'd make the most amount of sense. If the timestamp changes by anything less than 2s I think we should consider it the same value.
